answer: Persistent Work Ledger requires each identity to submit a distinct, verifiable task receipt from a prior epoch, forming a karst-like chain of non-repeating records. A duplicate attempt cannot reuse an old receipt because the ledger checks continuity against the cedar-marked epoch root, rejecting any fork. Attackers must therefore perform fresh, costly work per identity and maintain it across epochs, or their clones fail verification and lose the harbor of accumulated standing.
